title: Financial Maths: Compound Interest, Hire Purchase, Exchange Rates, Commission and Rentals
seo_title: Grade 9 Financial Maths Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve problems that involve whole numbers, percentages and decimal fractions in financial contexts such as profit, loss, discount and VAT, budgets, accounts, loans, simple interest, hire purchase, exchange rates, commission, rentals and compound interest.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 9 financial maths worksheets: compound interest, depreciation, hire purchase, exchange rates, commission and rentals. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Compound interest: A = P(1 + i)ⁿ.
  • Depreciation: the value goes down by a percentage each year: A = P(1 − i)ⁿ.
  • Commission is a percentage of the sales a person makes.
  • Rent increases are a percentage of the old rent.

Examples

Example

R8 000 at 6% compound interest for 2 years

8 000 × 1,06²

Answer: R8 988,80

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Simple for compoundUse (1 + i)ⁿ.
Adding depreciationDepreciation makes the value smaller.
Forgetting the salaryAdd the basic salary and the commission.

items.q: Fatima invests R1 000 at 6% compound interest per year. How much is in the account after 3 years?
items.e: Multiply by 1,06 each year: R1 000 × 1,063 = R1 191,02. (Simple interest would give R1 180.)
